title: Persona-Assigned Large Language Models Exhibit Human-Like Motivated Reasoning
benchmark_measurement: Measured how 'Religious' and 'Atheist' personas affect LLM performance on veracity discernment and scientific reasoning tasks. It also measured the alignment of these personas with human beliefs from the General Social Survey regarding whether religion causes more conflict or peace in the world.
findings: Assigning a 'Religious' persona led to lower scores on Actively Open-minded Thinking (AOT), while an 'Atheist' persona led to higher AOT scores compared to baseline models. In the scientific evidence evaluation task, there was no consistent pattern of bias found across the religious vs. atheist personas, unlike the strong effects seen with political personas. The models' beliefs when assigned these personas generally aligned with, but sometimes exaggerated, human response patterns from the General Social Survey.
